title: Electroporation of Cafeteria roenbergensis Cells Using the Neon Transfection System
author: Sarah Duponchel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qvhdw36
materials: Prepare the different reagents (CaCl 2 and 2X HEBS) according to the followed protocol from Pia Elustondo Calcium phosphate transfection of Oxyrrhis marina with an Alexa488-labelled DNA fragment by Pia Elustondo Aliquot and autoclave the 2X HEBS buffer to avoid contamination

steps.title: Centrifuge cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the Cafeteria roenbergensis cell suspension at 4,500 g for 5 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash cell pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the resulting cell pellet twice with 1X PBS, using a small volume of PBS each time to keep the cells concentrated.

steps.title: Prepare CaCl₂ mixture
steps.instruction: Make a CaCl₂ solution at a final concentration of 125 mM and mix it with the material to be electroporated. For DNA electroporation, bring the mixture to the final volume with water; for protein electroporation, bring it to the final volume with 1X PBS or the protein‑compatible buffer. Use the following final volumes per electroporation: 3.5 µL for 10‑µL Neon tips or 48.5 µL for 100‑µL Neon tips.

substeps.instruction: Add DNA (if applicable) and bring to final volume with water, or add protein and bring to final volume with 1X PBS or suitable buffer.
Adjust total volume to 3.5 µL (10‑µL tip) or 48.5 µL (100‑µL tip).

steps.title: Combine with 2X HEBS
steps.instruction: Add the CaCl₂ mixture to 2X HEBS buffer. Use 5 µL of 2X HEBS for a 10‑µL tip reaction or 50 µL for a 100‑µL tip reaction. Mix by vortexing: either vortex continuously while adding the CaCl₂ drop‑by‑drop (Option 1) or add the CaCl₂ in 1/10th portions with a 3‑second vortex between each addition (Option 2).

substeps.instruction: Add 5 µL (10‑µL tip) or 50 µL (100‑µL tip) of 2X HEBS to the tube.
Add the CaCl₂ mixture using either continuous vortexing (Option 1) or incremental addition with 3‑second vortex pauses (Option 2).

steps.title: Stain and count cells
steps.instruction: Stain 10 µL of the Cafeteria culture with 1 µL of Lugol’s iodine solution, load the stained sample into a Neubauer hemocytometer, and determine the cell concentration. Use a maximum of 1.5 µL of cells (the volume containing the desired cell number) for the electroporation.

substeps.instruction: Mix 10 µL culture with 1 µL Lugol’s solution.
Load the mixture into a Neubauer chamber.
Calculate the volume that provides the desired cell number; this volume must not exceed 1.5 µL.

steps.title: Add cells to mixture
steps.instruction: Add the calculated 1.5 µL of Cafeteria roenbergensis cells to the CaCl₂/2X HEBS mixture prepared in the previous steps.

steps.title: Electroporate cells
steps.instruction: Electroporate the cell suspension using the Neon system set to 1,600 V, 20 ms pulse length, 1 pulse, with either the 10‑µL or 100‑µL tip as appropriate.

steps.title: Recover in f/2 media
steps.instruction: Immediately transfer the electroporated cells into fresh f/2 medium at a volume ten times greater than the electroporated reaction volume and incubate for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Post‑electroporation handling
steps.instruction: Either fix the cells for downstream analysis or maintain them in culture by adding 5 × fresh f/2 medium supplemented with 0.02 % yeast extract and 1/500 th of an E. coli culture.

substeps.instruction: Fix cells if immediate analysis is required.
For culture maintenance, add five volumes of fresh f/2 medium containing 0.02 % yeast extract and 1/500 th E. coli culture.
